html:
The overthrow of Slobodan Milošević came on 5 October 2000, when hundreds of thousands of protesters converged on Belgrade and stormed the federal parliament after he refused to admit defeat in the presidential election.

The opposition candidate Vojislav Koštunica had won the vote of 24 September. Students of the Otpor movement, whose clenched fist logo later spread to protests abroad, had organised for months. Miners at Kolubara struck, and the police and army refused to fire on the crowds. Milošević conceded the next day. In 2001 the new government handed him to the Hague tribunal. The peaceful revolution ended a decade of war and sanctions and set Serbia on a slow road toward the European Union.
sum: The overthrow of Slobodan Milošević came on 5 October 2000, when hundreds of thousands of protesters converged on Belgrade and stormed the federal parliament after he refused to admit defeat in the presidential election.
